findings.title: Discovery: Live Host Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Document all discovered hosts and verify they are authorised to be present on the network segment.
findings.description: A host responded to ICMP ping or TCP probe during phase 1 host discovery. The host is alive and will be included in subsequent scan phases.
findings._x_remediation: Document all discovered hosts and verify they are authorised to be present on the network segment.

findings.title: Discovery: Open Port Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Review all open ports and close any that are not required for business operations.
findings.description: An open TCP/UDP port was detected on a live host. The service listening on the port will be probed for version information and vulnerabilities.
findings.impact: Each discovered open port represents a network service accessible to attackers. Identifying all open ports is a prerequisite for targeted service exploitation and provides the baseline for vulnerability assessment.
findings._x_remediation: Review all open ports and close any that are not required for business operations.

findings.title: Insecure Protocol Detected: TLS 1.0 Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable TLS 1.0 on the server. Configure a minimum of TLS 1.2. Prefer TLS 1.3.
findings.description: The server accepts TLS 1.0 connections. TLS 1.0 is deprecated due to known weaknesses including BEAST, POODLE, and weak cipher suites. PCI DSS 3.2+ requires disabling TLS 1.0.
findings._x_remediation: Disable TLS 1.0 on the server. Configure a minimum of TLS 1.2. Prefer TLS 1.3.

findings.title: Insecure Protocol Detected: TLS 1.1 Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable TLS 1.1. Configure minimum TLS 1.2 with strong cipher suites.
findings.description: The server accepts TLS 1.1 connections. TLS 1.1 is deprecated and does not support modern authenticated cipher suites.
findings._x_remediation: Disable TLS 1.1. Configure minimum TLS 1.2 with strong cipher suites.

findings.title: Insecure Protocol Detected: SSLv2 Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable SSLv2 immediately. Configure modern TLS 1.2+ with authenticated encryption cipher suites.
findings.description: The server accepts SSLv2 connections. SSLv2 is fundamentally broken and vulnerable to the DROWN attack (CVE-2016-0800), which can decrypt TLS 1.2 sessions.
findings._x_remediation: Disable SSLv2 immediately. Configure modern TLS 1.2+ with authenticated encryption cipher suites.

findings.title: Insecure Protocol Detected: SSLv3 Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable SSLv3. Enable only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
findings.description: The server accepts SSLv3 connections. SSLv3 is vulnerable to the POODLE attack (CVE-2014-3566), which allows decryption of CBC-encrypted TLS sessions.
findings._x_remediation: Disable SSLv3. Enable only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Ciphers: Weak Cipher Suite Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable all weak cipher suites. Allow only AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) with 128-bit or greater key length.
findings.description: The server supports cipher suites providing 64-bit or less symmetric encryption, export-grade key exchange, or null/anonymous authentication (RC4, DES, 3DES, EXPORT, aNULL, eNULL).
findings._x_remediation: Disable all weak cipher suites. Allow only AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) with 128-bit or greater key length.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Self-Signed TLS Certificate
findings.remediation_brief: Replace the self-signed certificate with one issued by a trusted CA. For internal services, deploy an internal PKI.
findings.description: The server presents a self-signed certificate not issued by a trusted certificate authority. Clients cannot verify the server's identity, enabling MITM attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Replace the self-signed certificate with one issued by a trusted CA. For internal services, deploy an internal PKI.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Expired TLS Certificate
findings.remediation_brief: Renew the certificate immediately. Implement automated certificate renewal (Let's Encrypt / ACME protocol).
findings.description: The server's TLS certificate has passed its expiry date. Expired certificates are rejected by modern clients with a hard error, and indicate poor certificate lifecycle management.
findings._x_remediation: Renew the certificate immediately. Implement automated certificate renewal (Let's Encrypt / ACME protocol).

findings.title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: TLS Heartbleed Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Upgrade OpenSSL to 1.0.1g or later. Revoke and replace server certificates and private keys. Invalidate all session tokens.
findings.description: The server is vulnerable to Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160). An attacker can read up to 64 KB of server process memory per request, potentially exposing private keys, session tokens, and plaintext data.
findings._x_remediation: Upgrade OpenSSL to 1.0.1g or later. Revoke and replace server certificates and private keys. Invalidate all session tokens.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Signing Not Required

mitre_attack.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay

findings.remediation_brief: Enable and require SMB signing via Group Policy: 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)'. Enable on all domain controllers and clients.
findings.description: SMB packet signing is not required on this host. Without signing, relay attacks (NTLM relay) allow an attacker to authenticate as any user whose credentials can be intercepted.
findings._x_remediation: Enable and require SMB signing via Group Policy: 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)'. Enable on all domain controllers and clients.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Share Accessible (No Authentication)
findings.remediation_brief: Disable null session access. Remove guest accounts. Enforce authentication on all shares. Audit share permissions.
findings.description: An SMB share is accessible without authentication (null session or guest access). Files and directories on the share are readable and potentially writable by unauthenticated users.
findings._x_remediation: Disable null session access. Remove guest accounts. Enforce authentication on all shares. Audit share permissions.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Share Accessible (Authenticated)
findings.remediation_brief: Apply least-privilege access controls to all SMB shares. Audit who has read/write access. Remove unnecessary shares.
findings.description: An SMB share is accessible using provided credentials. The share may expose sensitive files, configuration data, or provide a foothold for lateral movement.
findings._x_remediation: Apply least-privilege access controls to all SMB shares. Audit who has read/write access. Remove unnecessary shares.

findings.title: Uncategorized: LLMNR/NBT-NS Response Captured (Responder)

mitre_attack.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay

findings.remediation_brief: Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS via Group Policy. Enable SMB signing. Deploy 802.1X port authentication. Monitor for LLMNR/NBT-NS traffic.
findings.description: Responder captured an LLMNR or NBT-NS broadcast and responded with a poisoned answer. The victim host sent an NTLM authentication attempt to the attacker.
findings._x_remediation: Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS via Group Policy. Enable SMB signing. Deploy 802.1X port authentication. Monitor for LLMNR/NBT-NS traffic.

findings.title: Uncategorized: NTLMv1 Hash Captured

mitre_attack.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay

findings.remediation_brief: Disable NTLMv1 via Group Policy: 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' to 'Send NTLMv2 response only'. Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS.
findings.description: An NTLMv1 authentication hash was captured via Responder poisoning. NTLMv1 is trivially crackable in seconds using rainbow tables or GPU brute force.
findings._x_remediation: Disable NTLMv1 via Group Policy: 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' to 'Send NTLMv2 response only'. Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS.

findings.title: Uncategorized: NTLMv2 Hash Captured
findings.remediation_brief: Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS. Enforce SMB signing. Use Kerberos authentication in AD environments. Deploy a strong password policy.
findings.description: An NTLMv2 authentication hash was captured via Responder poisoning. NTLMv2 hashes are crackable offline with GPU-accelerated password cracking tools.
findings._x_remediation: Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS. Enforce SMB signing. Use Kerberos authentication in AD environments. Deploy a strong password policy.

findings.title: Authentication: Default Credentials Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Change default credentials immediately on all devices and services. Implement a credential management policy and enforce credential rotation.
findings.description: A service accepted a known factory-default username and password combination. Default credentials are documented publicly and exploited trivially.
findings._x_remediation: Change default credentials immediately on all devices and services. Implement a credential management policy and enforce credential rotation.

findings.title: Authentication: Working Credentials Found via Brute Force
aliases: Default Credentials Accepted on API Login Endpoint
findings.remediation_brief: Implement SSH key-based authentication and disable password authentication. Deploy fail2ban or equivalent. Enforce account lockout policy.
findings.description: Hydra discovered valid SSH credentials by brute-forcing the login service. An attacker can authenticate interactively and gain shell access to the target host.
findings._x_remediation: Implement SSH key-based authentication and disable password authentication. Deploy fail2ban or equivalent. Enforce account lockout policy.

findings.title: FTP: FTP Anonymous Login Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable anonymous FTP access. If FTP is required, enforce authenticated access. Prefer SFTP or FTPS over plaintext FTP.
findings.description: The FTP server permits anonymous login. Any user can authenticate without credentials and browse accessible files.
findings._x_remediation: Disable anonymous FTP access. If FTP is required, enforce authenticated access. Prefer SFTP or FTPS over plaintext FTP.

findings.title: Uncategorized: Known CVE Vulnerability Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Apply the vendor-supplied patch for the identified CVE. If no patch is available, implement compensating controls (WAF rule, network segmentation, disable the vulnerable feature).
findings.description: Nuclei's CVE template library identified a known CVE in a service banner, web application, or network protocol response. The specific CVE and affected component are recorded in the finding evidence.
findings._x_remediation: Apply the vendor-supplied patch for the identified CVE. If no patch is available, implement compensating controls (WAF rule, network segmentation, disable the vulnerable feature).

findings.title: Admin Endpoint Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict admin panel access to authorised management networks only. Implement MFA. Place behind VPN where possible.
findings.description: Nuclei detected an administrative interface (web admin panel, management console, or device configuration portal) exposed without IP restriction.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict admin panel access to authorised management networks only. Implement MFA. Place behind VPN where possible.

findings.title: Authentication: Default Credentials Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Change all default credentials. Enforce a password rotation policy. Add MFA to web-accessible management interfaces.
findings.description: Nuclei's default-login template confirmed a vendor-default credential pair is accepted by a web application or management interface.
findings._x_remediation: Change all default credentials. Enforce a password rotation policy. Add MFA to web-accessible management interfaces.

findings.title: Web Misconfiguration: Misconfiguration Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Review the specific misconfiguration identified in the evidence field and apply the vendor or CIS hardening guidance.
findings.description: Nuclei identified a security misconfiguration in a web application, server, or network service (e.g. debug endpoint enabled, directory listing, overly permissive CORS, missing security headers).
findings._x_remediation: Review the specific misconfiguration identified in the evidence field and apply the vendor or CIS hardening guidance.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: HTTP Security Header Missing
findings.remediation_brief: Add the missing security headers to the web server or application configuration. Implement a strong Content Security Policy. Enable HSTS with preloading.
findings.description: One or more recommended HTTP security response headers are absent: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings._x_remediation: Add the missing security headers to the web server or application configuration. Implement a strong Content Security Policy. Enable HSTS with preloading.

findings.title: Information Disclosure: Web Server
findings.remediation_brief: Configure the web server to suppress or obscure the Server header. On Apache: ServerTokens Prod. On nginx: server_tokens off.
findings.description: The HTTP Server response header discloses the web server software and version (e.g. Apache/2.4.51 or nginx/1.23.0). This aids reconnaissance and CVE lookup for attackers.
findings._x_remediation: Configure the web server to suppress or obscure the Server header. On Apache: ServerTokens Prod. On nginx: server_tokens off.

findings.title: Information Disclosure: Directory Listing Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable directory listing on the web server. Add an index file to directories that must be accessible. Apache: Options -Indexes. nginx: autoindex off.
findings.description: The web server returns a directory listing when no index file is present. File paths, names, and modification timestamps are exposed to unauthenticated users.
findings._x_remediation: Disable directory listing on the web server. Add an index file to directories that must be accessible. Apache: Options -Indexes. nginx: autoindex off.

findings.title: Injection: SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements. Apply input validation and output encoding. Deploy a WAF with SQLi signatures. Conduct a full application security review.
findings.description: sqlmap detected a SQL injection vulnerability in a web application parameter. An attacker can extract, modify, or delete database contents, potentially gaining OS-level command execution.
findings._x_remediation: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements. Apply input validation and output encoding. Deploy a WAF with SQLi signatures. Conduct a full application security review.

findings.title: Injection: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Apply context-aware output encoding for all user-controlled data. Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy. Validate and sanitise all inputs server-side.
findings.description: XSStrike or ZAP detected a reflected or stored XSS vulnerability. An attacker can inject scripts into pages viewed by other users, leading to session hijacking or credential theft.
findings._x_remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding for all user-controlled data. Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy. Validate and sanitise all inputs server-side.

findings.title: SNMP: SNMP Community String Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Change SNMP community strings from defaults. Restrict SNMP access by source IP ACL. Migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption. Disable SNMP if not needed.
findings.description: The device accepts the default SNMP community string ('public' for read or 'private' for read/write). SNMP data exposes network topology, interface statistics, routing tables, and device configurations.
findings._x_remediation: Change SNMP community strings from defaults. Restrict SNMP access by source IP ACL. Migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption. Disable SNMP if not needed.

findings.title: LDAP: LDAP Anonymous Bind Permitted
findings.remediation_brief: Disable anonymous LDAP bind in the directory service configuration. Require authenticated binds. Restrict LDAP query access to authorised service accounts.
findings.description: The LDAP server permits anonymous bind. Unauthenticated clients can query directory objects including user accounts, groups, and potentially password hashes.
findings._x_remediation: Disable anonymous LDAP bind in the directory service configuration. Require authenticated binds. Restrict LDAP query access to authorised service accounts.

findings.title: Discovery: Active Directory Domain Controller Identified
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure domain controllers are hardened per Microsoft Security Compliance Baseline. Restrict DC access to authorised management subnets.
findings.description: A host with open ports 88 (Kerberos), 389 (LDAP), and/or 3268 (Global Catalog) was identified as a likely Active Directory domain controller.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure domain controllers are hardened per Microsoft Security Compliance Baseline. Restrict DC access to authorised management subnets.

findings.title: Active Directory: Kerberoastable Service Account Identified

mitre_attack.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting

findings.remediation_brief: Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) with 120+ character auto-rotated passwords. Audit and remove unnecessary SPNs. Monitor for TGS ticket requests.
findings.description: Kerbrute or ldapdomaindump identified a service account with a ServicePrincipalName (SPN). Kerberos TGS tickets for SPNs can be requested without privilege and cracked offline.
findings._x_remediation: Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) with 120+ character auto-rotated passwords. Audit and remove unnecessary SPNs. Monitor for TGS ticket requests.

findings.title: Active Directory: AS-REP Roastable Account Identified

mitre_attack.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: AS-REP Roasting

findings.remediation_brief: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all user accounts. Do not disable pre-authentication without explicit justification. Enforce strong passwords on any accounts that require it disabled.
findings.description: A user account has Kerberos pre-authentication disabled. An AS-REP response can be requested and cracked offline without any credentials.
findings._x_remediation: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all user accounts. Do not disable pre-authentication without explicit justification. Enforce strong passwords on any accounts that require it disabled.

findings.title: Active Directory: BloodHound: Attack Path to Domain Admin Found
aliases: BloodHound: Attack Path to Domain Admin Found
findings.remediation_brief: Review and remediate the specific attack path(s) identified. Remove excessive ACL delegations. Apply the principle of least privilege to service accounts and admin groups.
findings.description: BloodHound-Python graph collection identified a privilege escalation path from a compromised account to Domain Admin rights, typically via ACL abuse, constrained delegation, or group membership chains.
findings._x_remediation: Review and remediate the specific attack path(s) identified. Remove excessive ACL delegations. Apply the principle of least privilege to service accounts and admin groups.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access: NFS: Export Accessible
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict NFS exports to specific client IPs in /etc/exports. Use root_squash and nosuid options. Disable NFS if not required.
findings.description: An NFS export is accessible without authentication or with world-readable permissions. Sensitive files on the export may be readable or writable by any network host.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict NFS exports to specific client IPs in /etc/exports. Use root_squash and nosuid options. Disable NFS if not required.

findings.title: RDP: RDP Exposed to Network
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict RDP to management VLANs. Require MFA for all RDP sessions. Patch against BlueKeep and DejaBlue. Use NLA (Network Level Authentication). Deploy RDP gateway.
findings.description: Remote Desktop Protocol (port 3389) is accessible from the network. RDP has a history of critical vulnerabilities and exposes the authentication surface to brute-force attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict RDP to management VLANs. Require MFA for all RDP sessions. Patch against BlueKeep and DejaBlue. Use NLA (Network Level Authentication). Deploy RDP gateway.

findings.title: Insecure Protocol Detected: Telnet Service Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Disable Telnet. Replace with SSH. If Telnet is required on embedded hardware, isolate on a dedicated management network.
findings.description: Telnet (port 23) is exposed on the network. Telnet transmits all data including credentials in cleartext. Any network observer can capture usernames and passwords.
findings._x_remediation: Disable Telnet. Replace with SSH. If Telnet is required on embedded hardware, isolate on a dedicated management network.

findings.title: FTP: FTP Cleartext Credentials
findings.remediation_brief: Replace FTP with SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) or FTPS (FTP over TLS). Disable FTP where possible.
findings.description: FTP (port 21) transmits credentials in cleartext. Credentials captured during banner grab or brute-force are fully readable by any network observer.
findings._x_remediation: Replace FTP with SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) or FTPS (FTP over TLS). Disable FTP where possible.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass: VNC Accessible Without Authentication
findings.remediation_brief: Enable VNC authentication immediately. Restrict VNC access to management networks. Use a VPN for remote access. Prefer alternatives with stronger authentication.
findings.description: A VNC service is accessible from the network without requiring authentication. An attacker has full graphical desktop access to the system.
findings._x_remediation: Enable VNC authentication immediately. Restrict VNC access to management networks. Use a VPN for remote access. Prefer alternatives with stronger authentication.

findings.title: Web Vulnerability: WordPress Vulnerability Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Update WordPress core, all plugins, and themes to the latest version. Remove unused plugins and themes. Harden WordPress per the WordPress Security Codex.
findings.description: WPScan identified a known vulnerability in the WordPress core, a plugin, or a theme. WordPress vulnerabilities frequently lead to RCE, data exfiltration, or credential theft.
findings._x_remediation: Update WordPress core, all plugins, and themes to the latest version. Remove unused plugins and themes. Harden WordPress per the WordPress Security Codex.

findings.title: Information Disclosure: Sensitive Path Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Remove sensitive paths from web root. Restrict access to admin paths via IP allowlist. Ensure .git directories are not served publicly. Audit all discovered paths.
findings.description: Gobuster directory brute-force discovered a sensitive path such as /admin, /backup, /.git, /config, /api/v1, or /.env exposed on the web server.
findings._x_remediation: Remove sensitive paths from web root. Restrict access to admin paths via IP allowlist. Ensure .git directories are not served publicly. Audit all discovered paths.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass: IPMI Authentication Bypass
aliases: IPMI 2.0 Cipher Suite 0 — Authentication Bypass and Hash Capture
IPMI Cipher Suite 0 Auth Bypass Confirmed
findings.remediation_brief: Disable IPMI Cipher Suite 0. Update BMC firmware. Restrict IPMI access to dedicated management VLANs. Require strong authentication.
findings.description: The IPMI/BMC interface is vulnerable to an authentication bypass (CVE-2013-4786 / Cipher 0 attack) allowing unauthenticated access to server management functions.
findings._x_remediation: Disable IPMI Cipher Suite 0. Update BMC firmware. Restrict IPMI access to dedicated management VLANs. Require strong authentication.

findings.title: Authentication: Default Credentials Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Change Oracle default accounts (SYS, SYSTEM, DBSNMP, SCOTT). Apply Oracle CPUs. Restrict listener access by IP. Disable remote OS authentication.
findings.description: ODAT discovered valid credentials on an Oracle database listener (port 1521). An attacker with database access can exfiltrate data or escalate to OS-level command execution.
findings._x_remediation: Change Oracle default accounts (SYS, SYSTEM, DBSNMP, SCOTT). Apply Oracle CPUs. Restrict listener access by IP. Disable remote OS authentication.

findings.title: Authentication: Default Credentials Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Disable the SA account or change its password. Enable SQL Server Audit. Restrict port 1433 to application servers only. Disable xp_cmdshell.
findings.description: msdat discovered valid credentials on a Microsoft SQL Server (port 1433/1434). Attackers can query data, execute xp_cmdshell, or use MSSQL as a pivot point.
findings._x_remediation: Disable the SA account or change its password. Enable SQL Server Audit. Restrict port 1433 to application servers only. Disable xp_cmdshell.

findings.title: Uncategorized: Public Exploit Available for Detected Version
aliases: Sploitus: Public Exploit Available for Detected Version
Metasploit Module Available for Detected Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Patch the affected service to the latest version. Implement network-level compensating controls until patching is complete. Prioritise remediation based on exploitability.
findings.description: Sploitus API returned a public exploit matching the service version detected during port scanning. The vulnerability is actively exploitable with publicly available tooling.
findings._x_remediation: Patch the affected service to the latest version. Implement network-level compensating controls until patching is complete. Prioritise remediation based on exploitability.

findings.title: Uncategorized: Metasploit Module Available for Detected Vulnerability
aliases: Sploitus: Public Exploit Available for Detected Version
Metasploit Module Available for Detected Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Patch the affected software to eliminate the underlying vulnerability. Review the Metasploit module documentation for exploitation conditions and implement compensating controls (network segmentation, WAF rules, IDS/IPS signatures) until patching is complete. Use the scanner module for non-destructive confirmation of exploitability.
findings.description: The Metasploit Framework contains one or more scanner or exploit modules matching a CVE identified during scanning. The presence of a Metasploit module significantly lowers the barrier to exploitation; unskilled attackers can use these modules without deep vulnerability knowledge. Scanner modules (auxiliary/scanner/*) provide non-destructive validation of exploitability. Exploit modules are listed for consultant reference only and are never automatically executed by Scattershot3.
findings._x_remediation: Patch the affected software to eliminate the underlying vulnerability. Review the Metasploit module documentation for exploitation conditions and implement compensating controls (network segmentation, WAF rules, IDS/IPS signatures) until patching is complete. Use the scanner module for non-destructive confirmation of exploitability.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: EternalBlue (MS17-010) — Host Confirmed Vulnerable
findings.remediation_brief: Apply Microsoft security update MS17-010 immediately. Disable SMBv1 via PowerShell: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false. Block port 445 at perimeter and between network segments. Verify patch status via WSUS or SCCM.
findings.description: The target host has been positively confirmed as vulnerable to EternalBlue (MS17-010). The SMBv1 implementation in the Windows SMB server does not properly handle transaction requests, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges. This vulnerability was weaponised by the WannaCry and NotPetya ransomware families and remains one of the most widely exploited vulnerabilities in existence. Successful exploitation requires no credentials and provides complete control of the target host.
findings._x_remediation: Apply Microsoft security update MS17-010 immediately. Disable SMBv1 via PowerShell: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false. Block port 445 at perimeter and between network segments. Verify patch status via WSUS or SCCM.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: EternalBlue (MS17-010) — Likely Vulnerable (SMBv1 + Unpatched)
findings.remediation_brief: Apply MS17-010 immediately. Disable SMBv1: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false. Validate patch status using the Metasploit auxiliary scanner (auxiliary/scanner/smb/smb_ms17_010) for definitive confirmation. Isolate host until patched.
findings.description: The target host exposes SMBv1 and does not appear to have the MS17-010 patch applied, indicating a high likelihood of vulnerability to EternalBlue. While this finding is based on banner analysis and SMB negotiation response rather than active exploitation confirmation, the combination of SMBv1 enabled and absence of patching indicators represents a critical exposure. EternalBlue (CVE-2017-0144) allows unauthenticated remote code execution with SYSTEM privileges on unpatched Windows hosts.
findings._x_remediation: Apply MS17-010 immediately. Disable SMBv1: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false. Validate patch status using the Metasploit auxiliary scanner (auxiliary/scanner/smb/smb_ms17_010) for definitive confirmation. Isolate host until patched.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMBv1 Protocol Enabled (EternalBlue Risk)
findings.remediation_brief: Disable SMBv1 via Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Lanman Workstation > Enable insecure guest logons: Disabled) or PowerShell: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol. Verify with: Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol.
findings.description: The SMBv1 protocol is enabled on this host. SMBv1 is a legacy protocol deprecated by Microsoft in 2014 that contains the vulnerability class exploited by EternalBlue (MS17-010). Even if MS17-010 is patched, SMBv1 contains additional weaknesses including susceptibility to NTLM relay attacks and other protocol-level vulnerabilities. Microsoft recommends disabling SMBv1 entirely on all systems regardless of patch level.
findings._x_remediation: Disable SMBv1 via Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Lanman Workstation > Enable insecure guest logons: Disabled) or PowerShell: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol. Verify with: Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass: IPMI 2.0 Cipher Suite 0 — Authentication Bypass and Hash Capture
aliases: IPMI 2.0 Cipher Suite 0 — Authentication Bypass and Hash Capture
IPMI Cipher Suite 0 Auth Bypass Confirmed
findings.remediation_brief: Disable IPMI Cipher Suite 0 in BMC configuration. Update BMC firmware to the latest version from the vendor. Restrict IPMI access (UDP 623) to dedicated out-of-band management VLANs with strict ACLs. Change all IPMI passwords to long, randomly generated values.
findings.description: The IPMI 2.0 implementation on this host accepts Cipher Suite 0 (null authentication), allowing an unauthenticated attacker to authenticate to the BMC with any password (CVE-2013-4786). Additionally, the IPMI 2.0 RAKP protocol leaks a salted SHA1 or MD5 hash of the remote management password during the authentication handshake, enabling offline password cracking even when Cipher Suite 0 is disabled. Successful exploitation grants full out-of-band server management access including console, power control, and firmware update capabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Disable IPMI Cipher Suite 0 in BMC configuration. Update BMC firmware to the latest version from the vendor. Restrict IPMI access (UDP 623) to dedicated out-of-band management VLANs with strict ACLs. Change all IPMI passwords to long, randomly generated values.

findings.title: SSH Vulnerability: SSHv1 Protocol Supported
findings.remediation_brief: Disable SSHv1 in the sshd configuration: set 'Protocol 2' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Restart the SSH service. Verify with: ssh -1 <host> to confirm SSHv1 is rejected.
findings.description: The SSH server on this host advertises support for the SSHv1 protocol. SSHv1 is cryptographically broken and contains fundamental design flaws including the ability to insert arbitrary data into SSH sessions and an information disclosure vulnerability in RSA key exchange. SSHv1 has been deprecated since 2006 and its use undermines the integrity and confidentiality guarantees of the SSH channel.
findings._x_remediation: Disable SSHv1 in the sshd configuration: set 'Protocol 2' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Restart the SSH service. Verify with: ssh -1 <host> to confirm SSHv1 is rejected.

findings.title: SSH Vulnerability: 'none' Authentication Accepted (libSSH Bypass CVE-2018-10933)
aliases: SSH Vulnerability: 'none' Authentication Accepted (libSSH Bypass CVE-2018-10933)
findings.remediation_brief: Upgrade libSSH to version 0.7.6 or 0.8.4 or later. For systems using OpenSSH this vulnerability does not apply — verify the SSH daemon in use. Apply vendor-supplied security patches immediately.
findings.description: The SSH server accepts the 'none' authentication method due to an authentication bypass vulnerability in libSSH (CVE-2018-10933). An attacker can send an SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS message before authentication is complete, causing the server to grant full authenticated access without any valid credentials. This affects libSSH versions 0.6.0 through 0.7.5 and 0.8.0 through 0.8.3 and provides complete unauthenticated shell access to any account.
findings._x_remediation: Upgrade libSSH to version 0.7.6 or 0.8.4 or later. For systems using OpenSSH this vulnerability does not apply — verify the SSH daemon in use. Apply vendor-supplied security patches immediately.

findings.title: SSH Vulnerability: Weak/Deprecated Cryptographic Algorithms
findings.remediation_brief: Update the SSH server configuration to restrict offered algorithms. In /etc/ssh/sshd_config set: Ciphers aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com; MACs hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com; KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512.
findings.description: The SSH server advertises support for deprecated or weak cryptographic algorithms in its key exchange, host key, cipher, or MAC algorithm list. This includes algorithms such as arcfour (RC4), 3des-cbc, blowfish-cbc, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1, hmac-md5, and hmac-sha1-96. Use of these algorithms exposes SSH sessions to potential cryptographic attacks and violates current NIST and vendor security guidance.
findings._x_remediation: Update the SSH server configuration to restrict offered algorithms. In /etc/ssh/sshd_config set: Ciphers aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com; MACs hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com; KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512.

findings.title: RDP: RDP Without NLA (BlueKeep) (MS12-020)
aliases: RDP Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) — BlueKeep Exposure
RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
findings.remediation_brief: Apply Microsoft security bulletin MS12-020. Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) as a compensating control. Restrict RDP access to authorised management networks. Block port 3389 at the perimeter firewall.
findings.description: The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) service on this host appears vulnerable to MS12-020, which includes CVE-2012-0152 (denial of service via specially crafted RDP packet sequence) and CVE-2012-0002 (pre-authentication remote code execution via malformed RDP packet). CVE-2012-0002 is a pre-authentication memory corruption vulnerability affecting the Remote Desktop Protocol in Windows XP through Server 2008 R2. Exploitation can cause a crash (BSOD) or potentially allow arbitrary code execution.
findings._x_remediation: Apply Microsoft security bulletin MS12-020. Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) as a compensating control. Restrict RDP access to authorised management networks. Block port 3389 at the perimeter firewall.

findings.title: RDP: RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
aliases: RDP Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) — BlueKeep Exposure
RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
findings.remediation_brief: Configure RDP to require TLS: set 'Security Layer' to 'SSL (TLS 1.0)' or higher in Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options). Enforce NLA. Apply a valid certificate to the RDP service.
findings.description: The RDP service is configured with a low or incompatible security layer, or does not enforce strong encryption. Configurations using 'RDP Security Layer' (as opposed to 'TLS' or 'Negotiate with TLS') use RC4 encryption that is cryptographically weak and susceptible to session interception. This allows a network-positioned attacker to decrypt RDP session traffic and recover credentials or session data.
findings._x_remediation: Configure RDP to require TLS: set 'Security Layer' to 'SSL (TLS 1.0)' or higher in Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options). Enforce NLA. Apply a valid certificate to the RDP service.

findings.title: RDP: RDP Without NLA (BlueKeep) (MS12-020)
aliases: RDP Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) — BlueKeep Exposure
RDP Weak or No Encryption Configured
findings.remediation_brief: Enable NLA via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Require user authentication for remote connections by using NLA. Set to Enabled.
findings.description: Network Level Authentication (NLA) is not enforced on the RDP service. Without NLA, unauthenticated network sessions are established before user credentials are validated, exposing the pre-authentication attack surface to vulnerabilities such as BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708) and DejaBlue (CVE-2019-1182). NLA moves authentication to the network transport layer, requiring credentials before a full RDP session is established.
findings._x_remediation: Enable NLA via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Require user authentication for remote connections by using NLA. Set to Enabled.

findings.title: Enumeration: NFS Export Points Enumerated — Potentially Unauthenticated Access
aliases: NFS Export Points Enumerated — Potentially Unauthenticated Access
findings.remediation_brief: Audit /etc/exports and restrict each export to specific IP addresses or minimal CIDR ranges. Apply root_squash to all exports. Remove exports that are not required. Restrict showmount queries by blocking RPC portmapper (port 111) and NFS (port 2049) at the network boundary.
findings.description: The NFS server responded to a showmount query and disclosed its export list. One or more exports are configured with overly permissive client specifications (e.g., wildcard '*', broad CIDR ranges, or no_root_squash), potentially allowing unauthenticated or minimally privileged network hosts to mount and access file system contents. Exposed NFS exports frequently contain sensitive data including SSH keys, configuration files, and application data.
findings._x_remediation: Audit /etc/exports and restrict each export to specific IP addresses or minimal CIDR ranges. Apply root_squash to all exports. Remove exports that are not required. Restrict showmount queries by blocking RPC portmapper (port 111) and NFS (port 2049) at the network boundary.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access: NFS Directory Listing Accessible
aliases: NFS Export Points Enumerated — Potentially Unauthenticated Access
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict NFS exports to specific authorised client IP addresses. Enable Kerberos authentication for NFS (sec=krb5p). Apply appropriate file permissions within the export. Consider migrating to SFTP or object storage for external file sharing.
findings.description: An NFS-mounted export directory listing was successfully retrieved, confirming that the export can be mounted and browsed from the scanning host. The directory contents, file names, permissions, and modification timestamps are visible. This confirms NFS access is possible and that the export is not adequately restricted by client IP, user authentication, or Kerberos-based NFS (krb5 security flavour).
findings._x_remediation: Restrict NFS exports to specific authorised client IP addresses. Enable Kerberos authentication for NFS (sec=krb5p). Apply appropriate file permissions within the export. Consider migrating to SFTP or object storage for external file sharing.

findings.title: Network Misconfiguration: SMTP Open Mail Relay Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Configure the SMTP server to reject relay for domains it is not authoritative for. On Postfix: set mynetworks to trusted IP ranges only, configure smtpd_recipient_restrictions to reject_unauth_destination. On Sendmail: configure access DB to deny relaying. Implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
findings.description: The SMTP server on this host will relay email for external domains, acting as an open mail relay. Open relays can be abused by spammers and phishing actors to send bulk email that appears to originate from the target organisation's IP space, damaging the organisation's email reputation, causing blacklisting, and potentially facilitating phishing campaigns. Open relays are identified by sending a test message from an external address to an external recipient via the server.
findings._x_remediation: Configure the SMTP server to reject relay for domains it is not authoritative for. On Postfix: set mynetworks to trusted IP ranges only, configure smtpd_recipient_restrictions to reject_unauth_destination. On Sendmail: configure access DB to deny relaying. Implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

findings.title: Enumeration: SMTP User Enumeration Possible via VRFY
aliases: SMTP User Enumeration Possible via VRFY
findings.remediation_brief: Disable the SMTP VRFY command. On Postfix: set disable_vrfy_command = yes in main.cf. On Exchange: VRFY is disabled by default but verify. Implement rate limiting and connection throttling on SMTP ports.
findings.description: The SMTP server responds to VRFY (verify) commands, allowing an unauthenticated client to enumerate valid email addresses and usernames on the system. The VRFY command returns a 250 OK response for valid addresses and a 550 response for invalid ones. This provides an attacker with a list of valid accounts for targeted brute-force, phishing, or credential stuffing attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Disable the SMTP VRFY command. On Postfix: set disable_vrfy_command = yes in main.cf. On Exchange: VRFY is disabled by default but verify. Implement rate limiting and connection throttling on SMTP ports.

findings.title: Enumeration: SIP Extension / User Enumeration
findings.remediation_brief: Configure the SIP server (Asterisk, FreePBX, Cisco UCM) to return uniform error responses regardless of extension validity. Implement SIP authentication on all extensions. Apply rate limiting and IP blocking for repeated failed registrations. Restrict SIP access to known client networks.
findings.description: The SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) service responds differently to OPTIONS or REGISTER requests for valid versus invalid extensions, enabling enumeration of valid user accounts and extensions. SVMap or a similar SIP scanner identified valid SIP usernames by observing differential server responses (200 OK vs 403 Forbidden vs 404 Not Found). Enumerated extensions can be targeted for brute-force authentication attacks to gain free VoIP calling or eavesdropping capabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Configure the SIP server (Asterisk, FreePBX, Cisco UCM) to return uniform error responses regardless of extension validity. Implement SIP authentication on all extensions. Apply rate limiting and IP blocking for repeated failed registrations. Restrict SIP access to known client networks.

findings.title: Web Misconfiguration: WebDAV Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable WebDAV if not required. If WebDAV is necessary, restrict it to authenticated users over HTTPS, limit access by IP, and audit PROPFIND and PUT/MKCOL method access in web server logs. On IIS: remove the WebDAV Publishing role feature. On Apache: remove the mod_dav and mod_dav_fs modules.
findings.description: The web server has WebDAV (Web-based Distributed Authoring and Versioning) enabled. WebDAV extends HTTP with methods including PROPFIND, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, and DELETE. If write access is granted to unauthenticated or low-privileged users, an attacker can upload arbitrary files including web shells, leading to remote code execution. Even read-only WebDAV can disclose file system metadata and source code.
findings._x_remediation: Disable WebDAV if not required. If WebDAV is necessary, restrict it to authenticated users over HTTPS, limit access by IP, and audit PROPFIND and PUT/MKCOL method access in web server logs. On IIS: remove the WebDAV Publishing role feature. On Apache: remove the mod_dav and mod_dav_fs modules.

findings.title: Network Misconfiguration: JetDirect / PJL Printer Accessible
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict access to port 9100 (JetDirect/RAW printing) using firewall ACLs to authorised print servers only. Disable PJL filesystem access commands in the printer administration console. Enable printer authentication and update firmware. Segment printers on a dedicated VLAN.
findings.description: An HP JetDirect or compatible printer management interface (port 9100 / PJL) is accessible from the network. The Printer Job Language (PJL) protocol allows reading and writing the printer file system, retrieving print job history, changing configuration settings, and in some models extracting stored credentials. Unauthenticated access to PJL is a well-known attack vector against printers exposed on corporate networks.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict access to port 9100 (JetDirect/RAW printing) using firewall ACLs to authorised print servers only. Disable PJL filesystem access commands in the printer administration console. Enable printer authentication and update firmware. Segment printers on a dedicated VLAN.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access: Redis Unauthenticated Access
findings.remediation_brief: Enable Redis authentication (requirepass) with a long randomly generated password. Bind Redis to localhost (bind 127.0.0.1) unless remote access is explicitly required. Use Redis 6+ ACL system to enforce per-user permissions. Block port 6379 at the network perimeter. Deploy Redis behind a VPN or bastion host.
findings.description: The Redis server on this host is accessible without authentication. Redis provides no access control beyond an optional password, and when exposed without authentication, allows any connected client to read, overwrite, or delete the entire key-value store. Redis supports commands such as CONFIG SET that can be abused to write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations on the server filesystem, commonly used to achieve remote code execution via cron job or SSH authorized_keys injection.
findings._x_remediation: Enable Redis authentication (requirepass) with a long randomly generated password. Bind Redis to localhost (bind 127.0.0.1) unless remote access is explicitly required. Use Redis 6+ ACL system to enforce per-user permissions. Block port 6379 at the network perimeter. Deploy Redis behind a VPN or bastion host.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access: MySQL Unauthenticated Access — Root with No Password
aliases: MySQL Unauthenticated Access — Root with No Password
findings.remediation_brief: Assign a strong password to the MySQL root account: ALTER USER 'root'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'strong_password'; Revoke remote root access: DELETE FROM mysql.user WHERE User='root' AND Host!='localhost'; Bind MySQL to localhost or a specific management interface. Restrict remote access with GRANT statements limited to specific source IPs.
findings.description: The MySQL server accepts connections as the root user without a password from the network. This grants an attacker full database administrator access including the ability to read, write, and delete any database, load/dump files to and from the server filesystem using LOAD DATA INFILE and SELECT INTO OUTFILE, and potentially execute OS commands via User-Defined Functions (UDFs). This represents complete compromise of database confidentiality and integrity.
findings._x_remediation: Assign a strong password to the MySQL root account: ALTER USER 'root'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'strong_password'; Revoke remote root access: DELETE FROM mysql.user WHERE User='root' AND Host!='localhost'; Bind MySQL to localhost or a specific management interface. Restrict remote access with GRANT statements limited to specific source IPs.

findings.title: Database: MySQL CVE-2012-2122 Authentication Bypass Risk
findings.remediation_brief: Upgrade MySQL to a patched version (5.1.63+, 5.5.24+, 5.6.6+). Apply the vendor security patch. As a compensating control, restrict MySQL access by IP using GRANT statements and firewall rules.
findings.description: The MySQL version detected on this host is potentially vulnerable to CVE-2012-2122, a memory comparison timing flaw in the authentication protocol. Due to a memcmp() optimisation in certain Linux builds and MySQL versions (5.1.x before 5.1.63, 5.5.x before 5.5.24, 5.6.x before 5.6.6), an attacker who sends the correct password approximately once in every 256 login attempts will bypass authentication. With repeated automated attempts, this allows authentication bypass for any known username including root.
findings._x_remediation: Upgrade MySQL to a patched version (5.1.63+, 5.5.24+, 5.6.6+). Apply the vendor security patch. As a compensating control, restrict MySQL access by IP using GRANT statements and firewall rules.

findings.title: Admin Endpoint Exposed: VMware ESXi
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict ESXi management access (ports 443, 22, 902, 5900) to dedicated management VLANs and bastion hosts. Disable ESXi Shell and SSH when not in use. Apply VMware security advisories and vSphere patches immediately. Enable two-factor authentication via vCenter. Join hosts to vCenter and manage via RBAC rather than direct host access.
findings.description: A VMware ESXi management interface (vSphere Client HTTPS on port 443, or ESXi Shell on port 22) is accessible from the network. ESXi hypervisors represent a critical attack surface: compromise of the hypervisor provides control over all guest virtual machines including the ability to power off, snapshot, clone, or extract disk images. ESXi has been a frequent ransomware target (ESXiArgs, Royal, BlackBasta), and exposed management interfaces are frequently exploited using known CVEs such as CVE-2021-22005 and CVE-2022-47966.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict ESXi management access (ports 443, 22, 902, 5900) to dedicated management VLANs and bastion hosts. Disable ESXi Shell and SSH when not in use. Apply VMware security advisories and vSphere patches immediately. Enable two-factor authentication via vCenter. Join hosts to vCenter and manage via RBAC rather than direct host access.

findings.title: RPC: RPC Null Session Permitted
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict anonymous RPC access via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options: 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled. Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled.
findings.description: The Windows RPC endpoint mapper accepts unauthenticated null session connections. A null session permits unauthenticated enumeration of shares, users, groups, and registry information via MS-RPC interfaces. This is frequently combined with SMB null session enumeration and forms a key component of unauthenticated Windows host reconnaissance, providing the attacker with Active Directory user account lists, group memberships, and domain SID information.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict anonymous RPC access via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options: 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled. Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Null Session Permitted
findings.remediation_brief: Enable the following Group Policy settings: 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled; 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' = Enabled; 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled.
findings.description: The SMB server permits null session connections — unauthenticated connections using an empty username and password. Via a null session, an attacker can enumerate share names, user accounts, group memberships, local policies, and domain SID information using tools such as enum4linux, rpcclient, or CrackMapExec. This information provides the reconnaissance foundation for subsequent targeted attacks including password spraying, credential brute-force, and Kerberoasting.
findings._x_remediation: Enable the following Group Policy settings: 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' = Enabled; 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' = Enabled; 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' = Enabled.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Administrative Access via Credentials
aliases: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
findings.remediation_brief: Rotate compromised credentials immediately. Implement LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) to randomise local administrator passwords per host. Disable the built-in administrator account. Enable SMB signing. Implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement pathways.
findings.description: Valid credentials were used to authenticate to the SMB service with administrative privileges, and access to administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) was confirmed. Administrative SMB access allows reading and writing files anywhere on the target filesystem, remote service/registry manipulation, and is the primary mechanism used by post-exploitation frameworks (Impacket, CrackMapExec, Metasploit) for lateral movement and remote code execution via PsExec, WMIExec, or SMBExec.
findings._x_remediation: Rotate compromised credentials immediately. Implement LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) to randomise local administrator passwords per host. Disable the built-in administrator account. Enable SMB signing. Implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement pathways.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
aliases: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
findings.remediation_brief: Audit all SMB share permissions and apply least-privilege access controls. Remove write access from any accounts that do not require it for business purposes. Implement monitoring and alerting on new file creation events in sensitive shares. Enable SMB signing to prevent NTLM relay to share authentication.
findings.description: An SMB share has been confirmed to be writable with the credentials used during the scan. Write access to a network share enables an attacker to plant malicious files, overwrite configuration data, introduce DLL hijacking payloads, or stage persistence mechanisms. If the share contains executable content served to other hosts, write access may lead to lateral movement or supply chain compromise within the organisation.
findings._x_remediation: Audit all SMB share permissions and apply least-privilege access controls. Remove write access from any accounts that do not require it for business purposes. Implement monitoring and alerting on new file creation events in sensitive shares. Enable SMB signing to prevent NTLM relay to share authentication.

findings.title: SMB Vulnerability: SMB Share-Level Authentication (No User-Level Auth)
findings.remediation_brief: Migrate to user-level SMB authentication. Configure the Windows workstation or server to use user-level access control: Computer > Properties > Sharing settings. Join the host to a domain and manage share access via domain user accounts and groups.
findings.description: The SMB server is configured to use share-level authentication rather than user-level authentication. Under share-level authentication, access is controlled by a per-share password rather than user identity. This model lacks auditability (no per-user access logging), prevents granular access control, and is incompatible with modern SMB security features including SMB signing and SMBv2/3 message integrity. Share-level authentication is a legacy mechanism associated with Windows 9x/ME workgroups.
findings._x_remediation: Migrate to user-level SMB authentication. Configure the Windows workstation or server to use user-level access control: Computer > Properties > Sharing settings. Join the host to a domain and manage share access via domain user accounts and groups.

findings.title: Active Directory: BloodHound AD Graph Data Collected
aliases: BloodHound: Attack Path to Domain Admin Found
findings.remediation_brief: Review the collected BloodHound data to identify and remediate high-risk attack paths (paths to Domain Admin, DCSync rights, unconstrained delegation). Implement tiered administration to limit exposure. Monitor LDAP query volume for anomalous bulk enumeration indicative of BloodHound collection.
findings.description: BloodHound-Python successfully collected Active Directory object data including users, groups, computers, GPOs, OUs, and ACLs and produced graph database ingest files. This data enables graph-based analysis of Active Directory attack paths, privilege escalation routes, and delegation abuses. The collection itself demonstrates that the network is reachable from the attacker's position with sufficient credential access to query LDAP at the level required for BloodHound enumeration.
findings._x_remediation: Review the collected BloodHound data to identify and remediate high-risk attack paths (paths to Domain Admin, DCSync rights, unconstrained delegation). Implement tiered administration to limit exposure. Monitor LDAP query volume for anomalous bulk enumeration indicative of BloodHound collection.

findings.title: Enumeration: LDAP Domain Users Enumerated
findings.remediation_brief: Implement LDAP query monitoring and alerting for bulk user enumeration. Apply Protected Users security group membership to privileged accounts. Enforce Kerberos-only authentication for sensitive accounts. Implement fine-grained password policies. Monitor for anomalous LDAP query patterns in Windows event logs (Event ID 4661).
findings.description: LDAP enumeration successfully retrieved a list of domain user accounts from Active Directory. The enumerated data may include usernames, display names, email addresses, account status, last logon timestamps, and group memberships. This user list provides an attacker with a validated target list for password spraying, credential stuffing, phishing, and Kerberoasting attacks. Successful LDAP enumeration often requires only a low-privileged domain account.
findings._x_remediation: Implement LDAP query monitoring and alerting for bulk user enumeration. Apply Protected Users security group membership to privileged accounts. Enforce Kerberos-only authentication for sensitive accounts. Implement fine-grained password policies. Monitor for anomalous LDAP query patterns in Windows event logs (Event ID 4661).

findings.title: Enumeration: Valid Kerberos Usernames Enumerated
findings.remediation_brief: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts to reduce the information disclosed in error responses. Monitor domain controller logs for unusual AS-REQ volume (Event IDs 4768, 4771). Deploy a SIEM alert for repeated KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN errors from a single source IP.
findings.description: Kerbrute or a similar tool enumerated valid Active Directory usernames by sending AS-REQ messages and observing Kerberos error code differences: valid accounts return KRB5KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED (18) or KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED (12/18) while invalid accounts return KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN (6). This technique does not require any credentials and works even when null sessions are disabled, providing a validated username list for subsequent password spray or brute-force attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts to reduce the information disclosed in error responses. Monitor domain controller logs for unusual AS-REQ volume (Event IDs 4768, 4771). Deploy a SIEM alert for repeated KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN errors from a single source IP.

findings.title: Authentication: Domain Accounts with Password Not Required
aliases: Domain Accounts with Password Not Required
findings.remediation_brief: Identify all accounts with the PASSWD_NOTREQD flag set: Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNotRequired -eq $True}. Set a strong password on each account and remove the flag: Set-ADUser -Identity <user> -PasswordNotRequired $false. Audit and enforce the domain password policy.
findings.description: One or more Active Directory user accounts have the PASSWD_NOTREQD (UF_PASSWD_NOTREQD, userAccountControl bit 0x0020) flag set, meaning the account may have an empty or blank password. Accounts with this flag are not subject to the domain password policy minimum length requirement and can be authenticated with an empty password. These accounts represent a trivially exploitable authentication bypass if empty passwords are present.
findings._x_remediation: Identify all accounts with the PASSWD_NOTREQD flag set: Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNotRequired -eq $True}. Set a strong password on each account and remove the flag: Set-ADUser -Identity <user> -PasswordNotRequired $false. Audit and enforce the domain password policy.

findings.title: Active Directory: Privileged Domain Accounts Identified
aliases: SMB Share Identified with WRITE Permissions
findings.remediation_brief: Apply the principle of least privilege: ensure privileged accounts are used only for administrative tasks. Enforce tiered administration (Tier 0/1/2 model). Add privileged accounts to the Protected Users security group. Enforce MFA for all administrative accounts. Restrict privileged account logon rights via GPO.
findings.description: LDAP enumeration identified user accounts with membership in highly privileged Active Directory groups such as Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Backup Operators, or Account Operators. These accounts represent high-value targets for credential theft, Kerberoasting, and AS-REP roasting. Compromise of any of these accounts typically results in complete domain compromise. The identification of these accounts guides further attack path analysis.
findings._x_remediation: Apply the principle of least privilege: ensure privileged accounts are used only for administrative tasks. Enforce tiered administration (Tier 0/1/2 model). Add privileged accounts to the Protected Users security group. Enforce MFA for all administrative accounts. Restrict privileged account logon rights via GPO.

findings.title: Web Vulnerability: WordPress Core Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Update WordPress core to the latest stable version via the WordPress admin dashboard (Dashboard > Updates) or WP-CLI (wp core update). Enable automatic core updates for minor versions. Review all active plugins and themes for compatibility before updating.
findings.description: WPScan identified a known vulnerability in the WordPress core installation. WordPress core vulnerabilities range from authenticated RCE and privilege escalation to unauthenticated information disclosure and SSRF. The specific CVE, affected version, and exploitation details are recorded in the finding evidence. WordPress core vulnerabilities are frequently weaponised within hours of disclosure due to the large attack surface and widespread deployment.
findings._x_remediation: Update WordPress core to the latest stable version via the WordPress admin dashboard (Dashboard > Updates) or WP-CLI (wp core update). Enable automatic core updates for minor versions. Review all active plugins and themes for compatibility before updating.

findings.title: Web Vulnerability: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Update the vulnerable plugin to the latest patched version via the WordPress admin panel (Plugins > Available Updates). If no patched version is available, deactivate and delete the plugin immediately. Consider a web application firewall (WAF) virtual patching rule as a temporary compensating control.
findings.description: WPScan identified a known security vulnerability in an installed WordPress plugin. Plugin vulnerabilities are the most common attack vector for WordPress sites, frequently including unauthenticated SQL injection, file upload bypass, XSS, CSRF, and remote code execution. The specific plugin name, version, CVE, and exploitation conditions are recorded in the finding evidence. Vulnerable plugins may be actively exploited using publicly available proof-of-concept code.
findings._x_remediation: Update the vulnerable plugin to the latest patched version via the WordPress admin panel (Plugins > Available Updates). findings.description: A deprecated network protocol is enabled on this host. Deprecated protocols lack modern security controls including strong authentication and encryption, have known cryptographic weaknesses or design flaws, and are no longer maintained by their developers. Examples include Telnet, RSH, RLOGIN, SNMPv1/v2, RIPv1, and older versions of SMB. The specific protocol is recorded in the finding evidence.

Use environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) for credential storage. Audit the web server document root for sensitive files.
